reason: The cited evidence (E1) examines oxidation of an equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn alloy at 400 °C, not the Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy at ~800 °C, and it does not address Ti oxidation, grain-boundary oxide formation, or the effects of reducing environments. Therefore, none of the key premises are supported by the provided evidence.
premises: Ti preferentially oxidizes at grain boundaries in this alloy at elevated temperatures
The resulting Ti-rich oxide scale is discontinuous, brittle, and poorly adherent
Spallation of this oxide allows oxygen ingress along grain boundaries, causing local embrittlement
A reducing gas environment suppresses this deleterious oxide formation
Suppressing the oxide improves intergranular cohesion and mechanical integrity
